subject: Hybrid cutover: anti-spoof filter + NAT reflection causing service reachability failures
messages:
From: Paul Brooks <paul.brooks@bluecrest-health.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@bluecrest-health.com
Date: 2027-06-11T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover

Hi Karthik,

We finished the hybrid cutover this morning and are seeing intermittent "connection refused" and 502s from our on-prem clients when they call the private inference endpoint (10.101.4.12). The control-plane metrics show requests arriving at the edge, but the backend reports "no route to host" for a subset of connections. We rolled back the DNS and some clients recovered.

Attached is a short tcpdump from a failing client and the observed NAT snapshot from our appliance. Can you advise? This is high impact — several clinician-facing flows are degraded.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Brooks
Sr. NetOps, Bluecrest Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Paul Brooks <paul.brooks@bluecrest-health.com>, ops@bluecrest-health.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-11T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover

Paul — thanks for the quick heads-up and the captures. I'm escalating to the cutover on-call. Initial read: I see asymmetric flows in the pcap (SYN from client -> edge, SYN-ACK arriving from backend IP that doesn't match the DNAT table). Two suspects: anti-spoofing / rp_filter on the on-prem gateway rejecting the return, or an unexpected hairpin/NAT reflection behavior at the edge.

Action plan (short):
- Marissa to validate DNAT/SNAT mappings and ephemeral port consistency.
- Lauren to check edge NAT reflection and whether hairpinning is enabled for the Bluecrest private subnet.
- Connor to run a connectivity trace with explicit src/dst and grab conntrack states.

Can you confirm which clients are still failing and whether the failing IPs are always the same? Also please keep captures coming if you see it.

I'll coordinate.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover

Quick findings from DNAT table on the edge cluster (cluster-e-11):
- DNAT rule for bluecrest: 10.101.4.12 -> 172.31.22.7 (backend) — looks correct.
- Observed translations show client src ports being rewritten as expected, but I see two translation targets for the same VIP: one via the local pod host route, one via the remote on-prem tunnel. That explains why replies sometimes go out a different path (return path asymmetry).

Attached: nat-translation-snapshot.json (filtered). If return traffic exits the wrong interface, on-prem rp_filter may drop the packet (anti-spoof).

Proposed short remediation: force return traffic for the VIP to egress the tunnel (policy-based routing) until we finish the cutover.

I'll standby for Connor's conntrack dump.

—Marissa
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover

I pulled conntrack from the edge box and remote auth-gateway. Key observations:
- Failing flow example: client 192.168.12.45:54012 -> VIP 10.101.4.12:443. DNAT -> backend 172.31.22.7:8443.
- conntrack shows ESTABLISHED state on edge with reply packets sent from backend IP 172.31.22.7 but egressing via the public-facing uplink instead of the on-prem tunnel.
- On the on-prem gateway, rp_filter (strict) is enabled by default and logs "source validation fail" for those return packets (source IP 172.31.22.7 hitting an interface that doesn't match).

Short-term mitigation applied at 10:32: policy route pinned for 172.31.22.7 -> tunnel0. Early signs look good for a few clients.

I also tested hairpin behavior by simulating a client on the on-prem net hitting the VIP: when hairpin is disabled, local clients attempt to reach the backend via the edge and fail because translation forces egress to wrong path. Enabling hairpin + consistent SNAT solved the local-client loopback in lab.

I'll coordinate with Bluecrest to temporarily relax rp_filter on the gateway (or allow the backend subnet) while we stabilize.

—Connor
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Paul Brooks <paul.brooks@bluecrest-health.com>, ops@bluecrest-health.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, edge-provider-support@edgefast.net
Date: 2027-06-11T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover

Paul — following up with a concrete short-term playbook so your NetOps can act without rolling back the cutover: 

Steps for Bluecrest NetOps (15–20 min):
1) On on-prem gateway(s) temporarily set rp_filter from "strict" to "loose" or add an exception for source subnet 172.31.22.0/24.
2) Confirm policy route for backend 172.31.22.7 -> tunnel0 is present on edge cluster (we will push if you can't).
3) On client-subnet test hosts, clear ARP and retry to avoid sticky ARP entries.
4) If you still see failures, enable hairpin NAT on the gateway for VIP 10.101.4.12 (we can provide commands).

We attached a short pcap (bluecrest-trace-0800.pcap) showing the return path mismatch and a proposed playbook doc with commands. If you approve, EdgeFast (copied) can temporarily flip the pointer on their side to ensure consistent egress.

I'll keep monitoring. We expect full remediation if the return path is pinned to tunnel0 and rp_filter relaxed for the backend subnet.

—Lauren Bishop
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Paul Brooks <paul.brooks@bluecrest-health.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-11T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Can't reach private inference endpoint after cutover — update

Team — quick update from our side after following the playbook:
- We relaxed rp_filter for 172.31.22.0/24 and applied the policy route to force backend egress through tunnel0.
- Observed client calls recovered within 3 minutes. No more 502s in the last 30m.
- We left hairpin disabled for now; local clients still reach VIP successfully after the policy route change.

We appreciate the fast triage and the proposed commands — saved us a rollback. Please keep this thread open while you submit the follow-up action items (playbook codified, permanent routing change, and a config note for future cutovers).

Thanks,
Paul
